messages.subject: Lavaan replication from MatLab
parts:
Hey all!

I am trying to replicate the results from MatLab for the following mediation and moderation models but I cannot get them figured out. Attached are the output from Matlab and the files. Below is my syntax for each of the models too. Does anyone know what I may be missing?

Thanks all!

Kyle

Mediation

model <- '
# direct effect
ReunificationwithParent ~ c*OutofHomePlacement + d*TypeofAbuse + e*ParticipationinParentingClass 
# mediator
Bonding ~ a*ParticipationinParentingClass
ReunificationwithParent ~ b*Bonding
# indirect effect (a*b)
ab := a*b
# direct effect
direct :=e + d + c
# total effect
total := e + d + c + (a*b)
'
fit <- sem(model, link="logit", data = Mediation)
summary(fit, standardize = T, ci = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit)
summary(fit)


Moderation

moderation_model <- '

 # regressions

  WeightGain ~ b1*CalorieIntake + b2*ExerciseProgram

  WeightGain ~~ b3*CalorieExercise'

sem1 <- sem(model = moderation_model,

            data = Moderation)

summary(sem1)

fitMeasures(sem1)

summary(sem1, standardize = T, ci = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Lavaan replication from MatLab
parts: That's a pretty cool name to have in the age of the Star Wars sequel trilogy :-)
Does anyone know what I may be missing?

The moderation syntax looks fine.  Does your output not match? 

The mediation output indicates that ReunificationwithParent is a binary output (one threshold), so you need to tell lavaan that:

fit <- sem(model, ordered="ReunificationwithParent", data = Mediation)

And you cannot currently request a logit link unless you use estimator = "MML"; otherwise, the default is the probit link (see the ?lavOpstions help page).  But that should match your matlab output, which has a threshold estimate (I assume that implies you are relying on the latent-response interpretation of the probit model, although strictly speaking the logistiic model also has that interpretation).  

Also, your matlab output does not indicate to what value the residual variance of ReunificationwithParent is fixed in order to identify the model, but the default in lavaan is the same as in Mplus: parameterization = "delta" implies the marginal variance of the latent response underlying ReunificationwithParent == 1.  If your matlab code is doing the standard approach for probit models (i.e., the linear predictor is transformed to a cumulative standard-normal probability), then that is consistent with the conditional / residual variance being fixed to 1 using the argument parameterization = "theta".  

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/CatMGLong.pdf

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.subject: Re: Lavaan replication from MatLab
parts: The moderation I am still having problems

You didn't explain what you think the "problems" are, but if you want to estimate the intercept, set meanstructure=TRUE in sem().  Also, the matlab output labels your caloric-intake variable "CALORIES_C".  If that means you mean-centered it, then the results might not match if you didn't also mean-center it before passing it to lavaan::sem().
